_comentario: How the kiosk UNDERSTANDS what people say in French (registro/Conversacion). What the kiosk SAYS is not here: it is in the catalog (context «totem», i18n/ba_fr.ts). The word lists are compared against the speech-to-text output once flattened (lowercase, without the accents in «aplanar» and with punctuation as spaces): so an elision is written with a space where the apostrophe was («c est correct», «je sais pas», «j ai»). Only «nombre» keeps the apostrophe («je m'appelle»). They can be written with accents: they are flattened when the file is read. A phrase is several words separated by one space; a hyphen is a space too («vingt deux», «moi meme»), so every number word here is a single word. What the kiosk says has to be answerable with these lists: the catalog confirmation (« Dites « oui, c'est correct » ou « non, c'est incorrect » ») with the ones in «respuestas». See docs/desarrollo/I18N.md, «Tótem: datos del idioma».

aplanar._comentario: Letter (UTF-8) → what it becomes when flattened. Anything not listed here that is not ASCII is dropped. A space: taken as a separator. The typographic apostrophe becomes the plain one (so «m’appelle» and «m'appelle» are the same). Guillemets and dashes are spaces.

numeros._comentario: Numbers said in words. «regla» «en» (Conversacion.cpp, grupo()): as in French, the hundred MULTIPLIES the unit before it («deux cents»; a bare «cent» = 100), followed or not by 1..99 («cent vingt»); a ten («trente») followed or not by its unit («trente cinq»: the hyphen is a space, so no «conectores»); or a unit (0 to 16). «mille» multiplies what comes before (or 1) and adds; «million» multiplies everything before. «ninguno» counts as zero. LIMITS of this rule for French: 17-19 («dix sept») are two words and give 10 and 7; «vingt et un» (with «et») gives 20 and 1, and 70-99 («soixante dix», «quatre vingt douze») are not composed: they need a French rule in grupo(). «digitos»: how each digit 0..9 is said, to read back a phone or an email (not flattened).

respuestas._comentario: Yes or no. First «noSabe» (neither yes nor no: ask again) and «noFrases» (a no even if it has a yes inside: «pas correct», «non c est pas bon»); then, if one of «si» or of «no» appears (and not both), that one. The first of each list is the one used when the model answers with a boolean.

_comentarioListas: cancelar, repetir and saltear: «exactas» = the whole utterance is that; «contiene» = it appears in the utterance (as whole words).

exactas: qu est ce que vous avez dit

contiene: je ne m en souviens pas

correo._comentario: The dictated email. «signos»: what is said instead of a sign, in order (multi-word phrases are replaced first, then single words). «noSonDigitos»: units of «numeros» that are not turned into a digit («une» is an article, not a number; «un» is kept as a digit because people dictate «un» for 1). «antes» and «despues»: what is said before the email («mon adresse c est») and after («merci»), which is removed. «terminaciones»: domain endings that, standing alone after the at sign, take a dot («gmail com» → gmail.com). «dominios»: a domain said without its ending that is completed. «decir»: how each sign is read back aloud.

telefono._comentario: «mas»: what is said for the + of the country code (only at the start); «decirMas», how it is read back. «repetir»: «double cinq» = 55, «triple zéro» = 000. «grupo»: how many digits are read and shown together; in France a number goes in pairs (06 12 34 56 78).

nombre._comentario: «antes»: what is said before the name, in order (the first one that matches at the start is removed, and again, until none is left). Here the apostrophe stays («je m'appelle»). «despues»: at the end. «noEmpiezaCon»: if the utterance starts like this, it is not a name («non merci»). «particulas»: lowercase in the middle of a name («Jean de La Fontaine», «Ludwig van Beethoven»).

opciones._comentario: Picking an option by its order: «orden» has, for the first, the second…, how it is named; «ultima», the last one.

_comentarioEtiqueta: etiquetaEnMinuscula: a field label said in the middle of a sentence starts lowercase («J'ai noté courriel…»; an acronym like «ID» stays).
